customer_updates.name: Vinayak Ghagare
customer_updates.text: Shreenagar Waterfall in Mulund is a hidden monsoon gem, perfect for a quick nature break with friends. Easily accessible via bus number 402 from Mulund station, it's just a 15-minute walk from the drop-off point near Shreenagar. The waterfall itself is beautiful during the rainy season, offering a peaceful natural setting surrounded by greenery. However, apart from the waterfall, there's not much else to explore. The area lacks proper amenities like food stalls or seating, so it's best for short visits. Despite its limitations, it's still a refreshing escape from the city chaos - just don't expect a full-fledged picnic spot.

featured_reviews.name: Sambhaji R Chopdekar
featured_reviews.review_text: After visiting Mandapeshwar caves, we decided to see the Eksar Veergal (hero stones) which is hardly 2 km apart. These beautiful hero stones have been in a private place of a residential building. The gatekeepers of that building are quite helpful, so entering there is not an issue. The place is also being used for feeding stray dogs however the gatekeepers assured us that they are harmless. featured_reviews.name: Narendra Lakhan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Eksar Herostone
Veeragal’ (Hero Stones)  have intricate carvings and are made of flat basalt. About 8-ft high, the stones were built as a tribute to warriors of the Shilahara dynasty navy.

The stones at Eksar date back to 10-12th century. The uniqueness of these stones is their depiction of Navy Battles.

This important heritage of Mumbai are unique in size and scale and it also a proof that Shilahara dynasty had naval capabilities.

The carved panels depicting ships and sailors  something rarely seen on hero stones, which usually depict land battles.

The Hero stones built up in 12th Centrury Shilahara dynasty and had a navy and fought a sea battle.

All the schools and colleges must take their children for such an excursion. On the top one can see Ghata Palav, a pot with dead man ashes as if the hero as an hero's welcome in the heaven with luscious damsels accompanying the hero. Herostones indeed! At Borivli west.
